simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Defending the `b1_recheck.lane_changes` field shape. The empty-array `[]` value this run IS the explicit no-upgrades-fired record — dropping the field per option (a) would silently lose the audit-trail signal that the mechanical recheck ran AND found zero downgrades, which is a distinct semantic from 'recheck did not run' (the absent-key state). The Gate 2 dogfood manifest of 002-develop-skill (block tbc-r1-f1, manifest line 71-72) made the mechanical recheck load-bearing precisely because reviewer judgement on the lane-aggressive flag was unreliable; the recheck record is the structured trace that closes that block. Empty-array vs absent-key is the same audit-trail-vs-silent-gap distinction the Phase 3 retro skill itself is designed to enforce (cf. PRD goal Outcome surface (d) zero silent failures). The field's downstream consumer surfaces with the FIRST run that fires a downgrade — at which point the field shape needs to already exist for the upgrade record to land in a consistent format; introducing the field shape only when it's first non-empty would force a schema migration on the scratch artefact mid-rollout. The simplicity-vs-traceability calibration here mirrors 002-develop-skill Gate 3 simplicity-r1-f1's defended push-back (T15 kept distinct because the cross-cutting contract anchors definitively): an audit-trail field whose empty value carries semantic content is not speculative configurability, it's a load-bearing trace surface. Separately, the simplicity reviewer explicitly granted that the 5-batch-split for 13 Green tasks at cap=3 is interview-grounded (PR-review-fatigue use case from 002-develop-skill Round 2 line 78), so that part of the finding is non-controversial and no push-back applies there.
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: No revision. The `b1_recheck.lane_changes: []` field shape is retained in lane-assignments.json with the empty-array semantic explicitly meaning no-upgrades-fired (vs. absent-field meaning recheck-did-not-run). The lane plan's b1_recheck.summary text already documents this distinction. The 5-batch split for 13 Green tasks is unchanged (interview-grounded cap, not speculative).

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: The asymmetric scope drift between T1 and T4 is real. Gate 3 surgical-r1-f1 tightened T4's cross-skill surface to runtime detection only; T1's parallel cross-skill surface (the `skills/develop/SKILL.md` Phase F.5 → F.6 hook itself) was not tightened in the same pass — T1 remained with `skills/develop/SKILL.md` as a code-edit surface in its tasks-file Scope. The lane plan's `files_touched: ['plugins/specflow/skills/complete/SKILL.md', 'plugins/specflow/skills/develop/SKILL.md']` for T1 mirrors the tasks-file Scope and inherits the asymmetry. Going with option (b) — defend T1's broader scope as in-scope for the auto-fire integration AND document the asymmetric tradeoff in the Gate 4 manifest. Rationale for (b) over (a): T1's auto-fire hook is the producer-skill landing surface (R1's per-task firing contract requires the `specflow:develop` Phase F.5 → F.6 boundary to invoke `specflow:complete`, and that invocation point IS code in develop's SKILL.md); deferring this to a separate enhancement PRD would leave `specflow:complete` v1 with no auto-fire surface (R1 unimplementable until the enhancement PRD lands). T4's `superseded_by_retro: false` default flag is structurally separable (data-default vs invocation-point); T1's hook is not. The asymmetric tradeoff is defensible.
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: Lane plan T1 `files_touched` retained as `['plugins/specflow/skills/complete/SKILL.md', 'plugins/specflow/skills/develop/SKILL.md']` AND T1 lane retained as `yellow` (medium blast from cross-skill touch is the correct triage outcome). Gate 4 manifest closing decision will document the T1-vs-T4 asymmetry as a known-and-accepted tradeoff: T1's auto-fire hook is the producer-skill landing surface and cannot be split from `specflow:complete` v1; T4's data-default is separable and was correctly routed to a separate enhancement PRD.

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: The unstated assumption is real and load-bearing. T9's lane reasoning binds verifiability=high to the `superseded_by_retro: true` boolean, but the field's existence on the existing task-history.json entry depends on the cross-skill prerequisite (specflow:develop Phase F.5 emitting `superseded_by_retro: false` as default) which is out-of-scope for `specflow:complete` v1 per PRD R4. The lane plan as written hides this dependency. Going with option (b) — extending T9's `lane_reason` text with the prerequisite clause — because option (a)'s `depends_on_external` field would introduce a new schema field across the lane plan that no other task uses, which is the speculative-configurability shape Simplicity correctly flags elsewhere. Option (b) preserves the existing schema and surfaces the assumption as prose.

Lane assignment unchanged (still green); the assumption is now named in the artefact, not silent.

The lane assignment is the AI's pre-execution judgement; the corpus signal `/insights` reads later lives in `task-history.json` per AC-15 of `specflow:develop`'s PRD, but the lane plan as a scratch artefact has no closed-loop verification. Going with option (b) — single top-level `feature_lane_outcome` field — because option (a)'s per-task `lane_outcome` field would duplicate signal already captured in the development-time fields written to `task-history.json` (specifically `lane_assigned` + `blast_radius_outcome`). The top-level summary is the surgical addition that closes the lane-plan loop without duplicating per-task data.

The lane plan does not surface this. Going with option (b) — a procedural pre-Phase-D announcement — because option (a)'s `batch_priority` field would introduce per-task ordering metadata that the orchestrator's batching algorithm should derive from `depends_on` mechanically (adding a redundant hint field is the speculative configurability Simplicity flags). Option (b) is the surgical procedural addition; the orchestrator's existing dependency-aware batcher already ensures T15 lands last, and the announcement closes the user-visibility loop on the partial-state risk.
